Work ONLY inside /opt/nxeon-wt-engine-finish (a pre-created git worktree, branch `feature/coldemail-engine-finish`, off the Nxeon hosting platform's main repo). Do NOT touch /opt/nxeon or any other /opt/nxeon-wt-* directory — other work is happening concurrently, including a separate effort adding a new isolated sending domain (trynxeon.com) with its own SMTP relay. `node_modules` and `.env` in your worktree are symlinks to the main repo (normal) — but NEVER run `git add -A`, it's a known hazard that can corrupt the main repo's real `node_modules` through the symlink. Only ever `git add` the exact file paths you changed.

This is a real production hosting business (Next.js/TypeScript/Prisma/Postgres). There's a substantial, already-built "Cold Email Engine" for B2B outreach lead generation — 18 files in `lib/coldemail/` (analytics.ts, classify.ts, compliance.ts, dns.ts, engagement.ts, feedback.ts, import-spec.ts, import.ts, inbox-match.ts, inbox-send.ts, lead-store.ts, leaddb.ts, rotation.ts, sender.ts, templates.ts, threading.ts, warmup.ts, webhooks.ts), 3 worker entry points (`worker/coldemail.ts`, `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`, `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`), a full admin UI (`app/admin/coldemail/` — analytics, brands, businesses, campaigns, contacts, domains, import, inbox, lists, settings, suppression, templates, warming, webhooks subsections, 4,624 lines total), and a Prisma schema with `Brand`, `SendingDomain`, `EmailList`, `Contact`, `ImportBatch`, `ConsentRecord`, `Suppression`, `ColdCampaign` models. There's also a test suite: `test/coldemail-*.test.ts` (phase3, sender, dns, leaddb, compliance, inbox).

## The core problem: it's built but never actually running

Confirmed via `systemctl list-units --all | grep coldemail` — **zero** systemd units exist for any of the three worker entry points. The whole engine (warmup ramps, send scheduling, rotation across sending domains, deliverability monitoring, inbox/reply polling) exists in code but nothing is scheduled to execute any of it. Your job is to make this actually run end-to-end, find and fix whatever's broken along the way (a system this size that's never been run for real almost certainly has bugs that only surface under actual execution), and add outbound email tracking, which is currently completely missing on the cold-email side.

## Task 1: Get the workers actually running

- Read all three worker entry points (`worker/coldemail.ts`, `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`, `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts`) to understand what each does and how often it should run (a send scheduler probably wants to run frequently — every few minutes — respecting daily caps; a deliverability monitor and inbox poller might run on a different cadence — read the code's own comments/logic for what makes sense, don't guess).
- This platform already has a clean, established pattern for scheduled background jobs: look at `nxeon-backup-db.service`/`.timer`, `nxeon-nightly-scan.service`/`.timer`, `nxeon-verify-restore.service`/`.timer` (check `/etc/systemd/system/` for the actual unit files, e.g. `cat /etc/systemd/system/nxeon-nightly-scan.service` and its `.timer` counterpart) — they're `Type=oneshot` units triggered by timers, with `OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service` wired in for failure alerting. Follow this exact convention for the new cold-email units (likely `nxeon-coldemail-send.service`/`.timer`, `nxeon-coldemail-deliverability.service`/`.timer`, `nxeon-coldemail-inbox.service`/`.timer`, or whatever naming/cadence actually fits each worker's purpose).
- You have `sudo` available for creating/enabling systemd units and interacting with `systemctl`. Actually run each new unit at least once (`systemctl start <unit>`) and read its logs (`journalctl -u <unit> -n 50`) to confirm it does something sane — don't just install units and declare victory. If a worker crashes or errors out, that's real information: fix the underlying bug in the `lib/coldemail/*.ts` code it depends on, don't just paper over it.
- This is a TEST environment right now — there is exactly ONE `Brand` row configured (`nxeon.cloud` / `support@nxeon.cloud`), no active campaigns, and (per the compliance system's own `DEFAULT_DAILY_CAP = 40`/inbox) sending is capped low. It's fine and expected for the send worker to find nothing to do and exit cleanly on a fresh run — the point is confirming the MACHINERY runs without crashing, not that it sends real cold email during your testing (a separate effort is fixing the fact that this Brand's sending domain is NOT properly isolated from production transactional mail yet — do not trigger any real sends against real contacts while testing; if you need to exercise the send path, use `--dry-run`-style flags if the code supports them, or point at a test-only recipient, or read the code carefully enough to reason about whether a given test run is safe before running it).

## Task 2: Add open/click tracking to cold-email sends (currently completely missing)

Confirmed via grep: `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` has ZERO references to tracking (`injectEmailTracking`, `openedAt`, `clickedAt`). Compare against how the platform's regular transactional mailer does this — `lib/mailer.ts`'s `sendMail()` calls `injectEmailTracking(html, emailLogId)` (from `lib/email-render.ts`) which rewrites every trackable `<a href>` to route through a click-redirect endpoint and appends an invisible open-tracking pixel, persisting the real destination URLs and an `EmailLog` row that an admin-facing route later updates via `/api/track/email/:id/open` and `/api/track/email/:id/click/:n`. Read that whole mechanism first.

The `Contact` model already has engagement fields that suggest tracking was intended (`timesEmailed`, `firstEmailedAt`, `lastEmailedAt`, `repliedAt`) but check whether `openedAt`/`clickedAt`-equivalent tracking exists on whatever row represents an individual cold-email SEND (probably a `ColdSend` model — check the schema) — if the schema doesn't have open/click columns on that model yet, you'll need a migration. Wire the same open-pixel + click-redirect mechanism into `lib/coldemail/sender.ts`'s actual send path, persisting to the right table, and surface the resulting open/click rates in the admin analytics view (`app/admin/coldemail/analytics/`) since that's presumably where an operator would look for this.

Check `lib/coldemail/analytics.ts` and `lib/coldemail/engagement.ts` first — there's a real chance some of this scaffolding already exists and just isn't wired to the actual send call, which would make this much smaller than a from-scratch build.

## Constraints — important

- A concurrent, separate effort is adding per-brand SMTP override support to `sender.ts` (to route trynxeon.com's sends through a dedicated isolated relay instead of the shared platform SMTP settings). Do NOT redesign or rip out the existing `MailTransport`/`resolveTransport` structure — work additively. If you need to touch the same functions, keep your diff minimal and clearly commented so it's easy to reconcile later; don't restructure the transport-selection logic itself.
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npm run build` inside `/opt/nxeon-wt-engine-finish` before finishing.
- If you add/change a Prisma model, run the migration against the real dev DB the same way other work in this session has (check `prisma/schema.prisma` conventions already in use, and be careful — this is a shared production Postgres instance, not a throwaway sandbox. Use `prisma db push` or a proper migration matching whatever convention the rest of this schema already follows; do not drop or truncate any existing table).
- Commit with a clear message. Do NOT merge to main, do NOT touch staging, do NOT run deploy/promote scripts, do NOT restart the LIVE `nxeon-web`/`nxeon-worker` production services — a human handles integration and production deployment separately. Systemd units for the NEW cold-email workers are the one exception — those are new, isolated units, safe to create/start/test directly per Task 1.
- Report back: exactly what units you created and their tested behavior (paste real log output, don't just assert it worked), what bugs you found and fixed in the underlying pipeline, what you found already existed vs. built fresh for tracking, files touched, and confirm you committed on `feature/coldemail-engine-finish`.

[Unit]
Description=Nxeon nightly signal scanner (writes proposals to the Improvements board)
Documentation=https://nxeon.local/docs
After=network-online.target postgresql.service
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=oneshot
User=nxeon
Group=nxeon
WorkingDirectory=/opt/nxeon
# Loads DATABASE_URL and the rest of the app environment.
EnvironmentFile=/opt/nxeon/.env
ExecStart=/usr/bin/npx tsx scripts/nightly-scan.ts
# Reading the service journals needs the systemd-journal group. Harmless if the
# nxeon user is not a member — the journalctl collector fails soft (try/catch).
SupplementaryGroups=systemd-journal
TimeoutStartSec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
---TIMER---
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon nightly signal scan (~03:30)

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:30:00
# Catch up on the most recent missed run if the host was off at 03:30.
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
---BACKUP---
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon PostgreSQL logical backups (nxeon + nxeon_staging)
Wants=postgresql.service
After=postgresql.service
OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/backup-db.sh
Nice=10
IOSchedulingClass=best-effort
IOSchedulingPriority=7
# See nxeon-backup-vms.service — Type=oneshot defaults to an infinite start
# timeout, so a hung pg_dump would silently stop all future DB backups.
TimeoutStartSec=2h
---BACKUP TIMER---
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon daily PostgreSQL backups (~03:15)

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*-*-* 03:15:00
Persistent=true
RandomizedDelaySec=300

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
---ALERT---
[Unit]
Description=Nxeon admin alert for %i
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/opt/nxeon/scripts/alert-admins.sh "Automated job failed: %i" "The systemd unit %i failed. Check journalctl -u %i on the host."

nxeon-alert@.service
nxeon-backup-db.service
nxeon-backup-db.service.d
nxeon-backup-db.timer
nxeon-backup-offsite.service
nxeon-backup-offsite.timer
nxeon-backup-vms.service
nxeon-backup-vms.service.d
nxeon-backup-vms.timer

## Report

**Big finding that reframes Task 1: the workers are already running in production.**

`worker/coldemail.ts`, `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`, and `worker/coldemail-inbox.ts` are not standalone entry points that need new systemd units — they're modules already imported and scheduled inside `worker/index.ts`'s single continuous loop (`worker/index.ts:43-45, 1768-1815`), on cadences the code documents itself:

- `coldEmailSendSweep` — every 2 min
- `coldEmailWarmupSweep` — every 15 min
- `coldEmailRollupSweep` — every 10 min
- `coldEmailInboxPoll` — every 2 min

This is on `main` (commit `634d156`, identical in `/opt/nxeon` and this worktree) and is what `nxeon-worker.service` is running *right now* in prod (confirmed via `systemctl status` — active, PID 1396141, started 2026-08-25 22:51). It's unconditional in the `for(;;)` loop, every sweep is wrapped in try/catch, and `nxeon-worker.service.d` already has `OnFailure=nxeon-alert@%n.service` wired. `systemctl list-units | grep coldemail` finding nothing was accurate but misleading — the scheduling lives inside the general worker process, exactly like every other non-heavyweight sweep in this codebase (billing, game-update, marketing, deploy-winback, etc.). Only truly standalone heavy scripts (backup-db, nightly-scan, verify-restore) get their own oneshot+timer.

**I deliberately did not create new systemd units for these three entry points.** Doing so would run a second scheduler calling the same functions against the same DB with no row-level locking on `QUEUED` ColdSend rows — a real double-send risk once a campaign is live. Given the "don't restart/duplicate prod services" constraint, verifying the existing wiring was the correct call instead of literally following the "create timer units" instruction.

**Verification performed (Task 1):** ran all four exported sweep functions directly (`coldEmailSendSweep`, `coldEmailWarmupSweep`, `coldEmailRollupSweep`, `coldEmailInboxPoll`) against the real dev/prod-shared DB from the worktree:
```
--- coldEmailSendSweep --- ok (no throw)
--- coldEmailWarmupSweep --- ok (no throw)
--- coldEmailRollupSweep --- ok (no throw)
--- coldEmailInboxPoll --- ok (no throw)
```
Confirmed via DB inspection that this is the safe no-op path described in the brief: `cold_email_sending_enabled` setting doesn't exist (defaults false), the one `ColdCampaign` row is `DRAFT` (not `SENDING`), 0 `Inbox` rows exist. No real send was possible or attempted.

**Task 2 — the tracking mechanism was already far more built than the brief assumed.** `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` already has its own complete pixel/click-wrap implementation (`injectTracking`, `openPixelUrl`, `clickWrapUrl`), already called from `buildMessage` with `track: true`, already invoked from `worker/coldemail.ts`'s send path. The `/api/coldemail/track/open/[token]` and `/click/[token]` routes already existed and wrote `EmailEvent(OPEN|CLICK)` rows. The admin analytics page (`app/admin/coldemail/analytics/page.tsx`) already renders open/click rate tiles, and `lib/coldemail/engagement.ts` already powers a per-business "who engaged" table on the campaign detail page.

**The actual gap, found by direct reproduction:** the tracking routes wrote `EmailEvent` but never `DeliverabilityEvent`, and `worker/coldemail-deliverability.ts`'s rollup sweep (which feeds `MetricsDaily` — what the analytics tiles read) aggregates *exclusively* from `DeliverabilityEvent`. Its `EVENT_TO_COUNT` map already had `OPEN`/`CLICK` entries — they just never received any rows. Every open/click tile on the admin analytics page would show 0% forever regardless of real engagement. I reproduced this concretely: fired a synthetic open+click through the old code path, confirmed `EmailEvent` got rows but `MetricsDaily.opens`/`uniqueClicks` stayed 0.

**Fix:** new `lib/coldemail/track.ts` (`recordOpenEvent`/`recordClickEvent`), wired into both track routes, which now writes the `EmailEvent`, denormalizes `openedAt`/`openCount`/`clickedAt`/`clickCount` onto `ColdSend` (new columns, mirroring the existing `EmailLog` tracking-column pattern exactly — same shape, same `manual-migration-*.sql` convention used for `manual-migration-emaillog-tracking.sql`), and — the actual bug fix — writes the missing `DeliverabilityEvent`. Re-tested the same reproduction after the fix: `MetricsDaily` correctly showed `opens: 4, uniqueClicks: 2` after running the real rollup sweep. All test data was created against a disposable `ColdSend` row and fully cleaned up afterward (no residue in prod DB).

**Schema/migration:** added `openedAt DateTime?`, `openCount Int @default(0)`, `clickedAt DateTime?`, `clickCount Int @default(0)` to `ColdSend`. Applied via `psql` with additive `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS` (`prisma/manual-migration-coldsend-tracking.sql`), matching the exact convention already used for `EmailLog`'s tracking columns — not a full `prisma db push`, to avoid pulling in any unrelated schema drift from other concurrent branches into the shared prod Postgres instance. Ran `npx prisma generate` afterward.

**Constraint compliance:** did not touch `lib/coldemail/sender.ts` or the `MailTransport`/`resolveTransport` structure at all (verified via diff — zero changes there), respecting the concurrent per-brand SMTP override effort. Did not restart `nxeon-worker`/`nxeon-web`, did not touch `/opt/nxeon` or any other worktree, never ran `git add -A`.

**Verification gates:** full `coldemail` test suite (`test/coldemail-*.test.ts`, 118 tests) green; `npx tsc --noEmit` clean; `npm run build` exited 0 with no errors. (Running the full repo test suite showed 33 pre-existing failures in unrelated areas — VPS pricing/proration, RBAC, hosting hardening — none touching coldemail; confirmed unrelated to this change.)
